aspects.says: The @Override check runs only when the subclass compiles; a class compiled against one version of its supertype and run against another gets no check, and the supertype's method runs.
basis: section:@Override Turns a Method That Stopped Overriding into a Compile Error

aspects.says: With @Override, javac rejects a method that matches no supertype method, so a supertype change or a misspelt name fails the build instead of leaving a new method that nothing calls.
basis: section:@Override Turns a Method That Stopped Overriding into a Compile Error
aspects.reason: javac enforces it, so no wrong solution compiles and can be graded at run time; the quiz checks the run-time side, a method that silently stopped overriding

aspects.says: @SuppressWarnings("deprecation") doesn't silence a [removal] warning, which needs "removal"; a deprecated caller and an overriding method still get removal warnings.
basis: section:A Use of a forRemoval Element Warns by Default; Plain Deprecation Is Only a Note

aspects.says: javac reports each use of a forRemoval element as a [removal] warning by default, while plain deprecated uses are folded into a note that -Werror doesn't count until -Xlint:deprecation lists them.
basis: section:A Use of a forRemoval Element Warns by Default; Plain Deprecation Is Only a Note

aspects.says: javac doesn't check the @SafeVarargs promise: a method that keeps or hands out its varargs array pollutes the heap, and the ClassCastException lands in code with no cast, away from the cause.
basis: section:@SafeVarargs Removes the Warning at the Cause, and javac Doesn't Check the Promise

aspects.says: @SafeVarargs stops javac warning every caller about generic array creation, which @SuppressWarnings on the declaration doesn't do.
basis: section:@SafeVarargs Removes the Warning at the Cause, and javac Doesn't Check the Promise

aspects.says: A suppression covers everything inside the declaration that carries it, including code added later; on a local variable it covers one declaration.
basis: section:@SuppressWarnings Covers Its Whole Declaration, Including Warnings Added Later

aspects.says: A cast to a parameterized type checks only the class, so code that converts untyped input checks each element and needs no suppression; otherwise the ClassCastException comes later, at a read with no cast.
basis: section:@SuppressWarnings Covers Its Whole Declaration, Including Warnings Added Later

aspects.says: javac ignores @SuppressWarnings keys it doesn't know, "all" included, without a warning.
basis: section:@SuppressWarnings Covers Its Whole Declaration, Including Warnings Added Later

aspects.says: The [varargs] lint flags any use of the varargs array other than an element read, so it flags a copy and a leak alike.
basis: section:@SafeVarargs Removes the Warning at the Cause, and javac Doesn't Check the Promise
aspects.reason: a lint report, not run-time behaviour; the page shows it on the faulty and the fixed factory
